episodes.title: The Cosmic Turtle
episodes.subjectDescription: A world-bearing cosmic turtle reimagined as a mobile, closed-loop orbital habitat designed to carry 10,000 residents for a century.
episodes.hotspot: Metals carry 61.0% of the approved cradle-to-commissioning baseline.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 360 m world-bearing habitat commissioned at an orbital shipyard gate: 1.00 Mt CO₂e before operation, with metals carrying 61.0% of the approved baseline.
episodes.functionalUnit: Build and commission one 360 m world-bearing habitat at an orbital shipyard gate, designed for 10,000 residents and a 100-year service life. Construction burdens only.

evidence.basis: The approved episode reconstructs one 360 m world-bearing habitat with a 220 m habitat disc, a 260 × 210 m shell plan and a commissioned mass of 1.268 Mt. The declared cradle-to-commissioning inventory includes 215,000 t of structural metal, 420,000 t of concrete, glass, electrical systems, habitat finishes, a 550,000 t initial soil-and-water charge, 650 GWh of orbital-yard electricity and 2.079 billion t·km of additional freight. All quantities are explicit engineering assumptions for a non-existent orbital supply chain.
evidence.uncertainty: Structural-metal mass and metal origin are the published sensitivity levers. Changing only metal mass moves the result from 0.878 to 1.120 Mt CO₂e around the 1.00 Mt baseline; changing only the closed-loop share moves it from 1.21 Mt at 0% closed-loop metal to 0.836 Mt at 80%.

assessment.referenceFlow: Build and commission one 360 m world-bearing habitat at an orbital shipyard gate, designed for 10,000 residents and a 100-year service life. Construction burdens only.
assessment.temporalContext: One construction-and-commissioning event for a habitat designed for a 100-year service life.
assessment.geographicContext: An orbital shipyard gate in a non-existent orbital supply chain.
assessment.cutoffSummary: The model stops when the complete ark is commissioned at the orbital shipyard gate; orbital lift, operation, propulsion, maintenance, replacements, end of life and credits remain outside the boundary.

episodes.title: El Dorado
episodes.subjectDescription: The legendary golden kingdom reframed as one ceremonial investiture at Lake Guatavita, centred on a gilded ruler and offerings cast into the water.
episodes.hotspot: Primary gold contributes 99.93% of the approved baseline; all other modeled flows contribute 0.07% combined.
episodes.featuredDescription: One staged investiture rite at Lake Guatavita: 1,287 t CO₂e, with 50.5 kg of primary gold contributing 99.93% of the approved baseline.
episodes.functionalUnit: One staged investiture rite at Lake Guatavita, modeled from material supply to ceremonial launch, with 50.5 kg of primary gold assigned as unrecovered ceremonial use.

evidence.basis: The approved episode models one staged investiture rite at Lake Guatavita, anchored to the Muisca raft tradition rather than a literal city of gold. The declared reconstruction uses a 6.0 × 3.0 m, 800 kg softwood raft; 50.5 kg of primary gold dust and offerings; 0.02 t of textiles and cords; 120 kWh workshop electricity; 60 L site diesel; 168 t·km road freight; and 2 m³ washdown water. The boundary stops at ceremonial launch, and the gold is treated as unrecovered use with no recovery, recycling or salvage credit.
evidence.uncertainty: Gold mass and primary-gold emissions intensity are the published sensitivity levers. Changing only gold mass moves the total from 268 t CO₂e for 10.5 kg to 2,560 t CO₂e for 100.5 kg around the 50.5 kg baseline. Changing only the gold factor moves the total from 132 to 1,608 t CO₂e around the 1,287 t baseline; timber, energy, freight and water remain fixed in those scenarios.

episodes.editorialDescriptor: Impossible stories, reconstructed as traceable systems.

assessment.geographicContext: Lake Guatavita, from material supply to the ceremonial launch point.

episodes.title: Valhalla
episodes.subjectDescription: Odin's immense hall for chosen warriors, reconstructed as a circular timber complex with 540 gates, a shield roof and spear-lined walls.
episodes.hotspot: Wood and timber products contribute 74.3% of the approved baseline; iron and steel contribute 13.5%, and material freight 8.7%.
episodes.featuredDescription: One reconstructed Valhalla structural shell sized for the first muster of 432,000 einherjar: 607.8 kt CO₂e, with wood and timber products contributing 74.3% of the approved baseline.
episodes.functionalUnit: One reconstructed Valhalla structural shell sized to stage 432,000 einherjar through 540 gates for the first muster.

evidence.basis: The approved episode defines the first muster of 432,000 einherjar through 540 gates, with 800 armed warriors passing abreast through each gate. A 0.65 m warrior pitch sets a 520 m clear gate width; the declared circular-hall proxy then gives a 308,880 m perimeter, 98.3 km equivalent diameter, 7.41 million m² roofed floor area, 9.64 million m² sloped roof area and 2.08 million t material mass. The inventory includes the timber shell, steel artefacts, stone base, construction electricity, material freight and one commissioning feast, using the episode’s declared 2026 UK Government factors and proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: Warrior pitch and steel proxy choice are the published sensitivity levers. Changing only warrior pitch from 0.55 m to 0.75 m moves the result from 517.2 to 698.3 kt CO₂e around the 607.8 kt baseline. Changing only the steel proxy from 1,822 to 3,822 kg CO₂e/t moves the result from 577.9 to 635.3 kt CO₂e, without displacing timber as the hotspot.

episodes.title: The Jars of the Danaids
episodes.subjectDescription: Fifty condemned Danaids repeatedly carry water in perforated jars toward a bottomless cistern, turning punishment into an endless cycle of loss.
episodes.hotspot: Managed water supply and treatment contribute 96.9% of the approved baseline; the annualized hydriae contribute 0.9%.
episodes.featuredDescription: One reconstructed operating year of the Danaids’ punishment: 1.36 t CO₂e, with managed water supply and treatment contributing 96.9% of the approved baseline.
episodes.functionalUnit: One reconstructed operating year of the Danaids’ punishment.

evidence.basis: The approved episode defines one reconstructed operating year for 50 Danaids using 50 perforated hydriae. Museum hydria evidence anchors the ovoid form; the 0.54 m height, 3.2 kg dry mass, three-year vessel life, 3,650 m³/y managed-water flow, 730 m³/y target attempt, 80% jar loss, 0.120 t stone basin, 0.027 t timber staging, 60 kWh repair electricity and 16 t·km freight are declared reconstruction inputs. Fired clay is modelled with the 2026 UK Government bricks proxy; the remaining emitting flows use the episode’s declared 2026 UK Government factors.
evidence.uncertainty: Leakage rate and water-source model are the published sensitivity levers. Changing only jar leakage from 65% to 90% moves the result from 0.798 to 2.687 t CO₂e/year. Changing only the water-source model moves it from 0.043 t CO₂e/year for a zero-emission mythic spring to 2.349 t CO₂e/year for the desalinated-water proxy.

episodes.title: The Augean Stables
episodes.subjectDescription: Heracles' one-day cleansing of the Augean cattle yards by diverting river water through temporary channels and returning the site to service.
episodes.hotspot: Earthmoving fuel contributes 71.7% of the approved baseline; materials contribute 18.1% and equipment mobilization 10.2%.
episodes.featuredDescription: One complete river-assisted clearing campaign at Elis: 181 t CO₂e, with earthmoving fuel contributing 71.7% of the approved baseline while gravity-fed river water carries no pumping burden in the model.
episodes.functionalUnit: One complete river-assisted clearing campaign removing the modelled inherited stock and returning the yard, temporary channels and ordinary river courses to serviceable condition within one daylight period at Elis, including an 8-hour wash.

evidence.basis: The approved episode freezes a 300 × 120 m stable plan, 2.20 m waste depth, 79,200 m³ inherited stock, 51,480 t wet mass and 52,500 m³ of campaign earthworks. The model includes temporary intake and outlet channels, earthmoving and site restoration, timber gates and metal fittings, foundation breach and repair, equipment mobilization and fuel. The two rivers pass 100 m³/s for eight hours without pumping. Six emitting flows use the episode’s declared 2026 UK Government factors or material-use proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: Channel geometry and fuel pathway are the published sensitivity levers. Changing only earthwork volume moves the result from 148 to 220 t CO₂e, while changing the 40,550 L fuel pathway moves it from 75.5 t CO₂e with HVO to 184 t CO₂e with 100% mineral diesel. Greece-specific non-road factors were unavailable, so UK 2026 factors are applied transparently outside their native reporting context.

assessment.temporalContext: One daylight clearing campaign including an eight-hour river wash and restoration of the yard, channels and ordinary river courses.

episodes.subjectDescription: The miraculous horn of plenty treated as a ceremonial vessel presenting one tonne of mixed bounty during a day at the Achelous sanctuary.
episodes.hotspot: Food production contributes 99.1% of the approved baseline; food-waste treatment contributes 0.9%, while vessel, utilities and delivery together remain below 0.01%.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 24-hour Cornucopia service presenting 1.00 t of mixed food: 3.74 t CO₂e, with food production contributing 99.1% while vessel, utilities and delivery remain below 0.01%.
episodes.functionalUnit: One 24-hour cornucopia service presenting 1,000 kg of mixed food at the point of use, including treatment of 5% residual food waste.

evidence.basis: The approved episode defines one 24-hour cornucopia service at the Achelous sanctuary presenting 1.00 t of mixed food and treating 50 kg of residual food waste. It reconstructs a 1.20 m curved horn with a 0.48 m mouth, 8 mm wall, 11.7 kg shell and 13.5 kg total mass, allocated across 100 uses. The broken horn enters at zero burden; bronze, workshop electricity, water, road freight and residual treatment use the episode's declared UK Government 2026 factor families. evidence.uncertainty: The magical mechanism has no assigned flow and is explicitly treated as uncertainty rather than zero impact. The published physical sensitivity moves the result from 1.87 to 7.47 t CO₂e as output changes from 0.50 to 2.00 t, while the published menu-composition cases span 1.11 to 13.4 t CO₂e per service at the same one-tonne output.

episodes.featuredDescription: Maintain one 30-oared ceremonial hull at Piraeus for 100 years: 23.6 t CO₂e, with structural wood contributing 45.6% and 82.5% of the footprint occurring after launch.
episodes.functionalUnit: Maintain one 30-oared ceremonial hull in structurally seaworthy condition at Piraeus for 100 years.

evidence.basis: The approved episode defines one 30-oared ceremonial hull at Piraeus and freezes an engineering reconstruction at 20 m overall length, 3.4 m beam, 1.1 m moulded depth, 8.00 t of initial structural wood, 0.25 t of initial metal fasteners and 0.30 t of pitch. The geometry is explicitly not an archaeological claim. DEFRA 2026 material, electricity, freight and waste-routing factors are used as declared modern proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: The 25-year full-equivalent structural replacement interval drives every replacement-linked flow. The approved physical sensitivity moves the result from 17.9 to 33.7 t CO₂e across 40- to 15-year intervals, while changing only the timber factor moves it from 14.4 to 29.0 t CO₂e.

episodes.title: Gungnir
episodes.subjectDescription: Odin's unerring spear reconstructed as a durable iron-headed weapon with a European ash shaft and proportions anchored to Viking-Age examples.
episodes.hotspot: Forge heat contributes 51.8% of the approved baseline footprint, more than the iron head at 30.6%.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 2.40 m Gungnir-class spear, manufactured and delivered once: 3.01 kg CO₂e, with forge heat contributing 51.8% and the iron head 30.6% of the approved baseline.
episodes.functionalUnit: Provide one durable Gungnir-class spear, delivered ready for repeated ceremonial and combat use. The model covers one manufacturing-and-delivery event; use and end-of-life remain outside the boundary.

evidence.basis: The approved episode freezes a 2.40 m, 1.30 kg Gungnir-class spear before inventory, with a 0.370 m / 0.322 kg iron head anchored to British Museum object 1868,0128.2 and a 0.976 kg European ash shaft reconstructed from geometry and density. The five contributing flows use declared 2026 UK Government GHG factor families for a primary ferrous-material proxy, primary wood, propane plus WTT, UK electricity plus T&D and WTT, and average HGV freight plus WTT.
evidence.uncertainty: The 6 kWh forge-heat demand is an engineering assumption and the 500 km delivery distance is a narrative proxy. The published forge-heat sensitivity moves the total from 2.23 to 4.57 kg CO₂e, while the ferrous-material factor sensitivity spans 2.68 to 3.32 kg CO₂e; the heat-demand assumption is the larger uncertainty lever.

episodes.functionalUnit: One freestanding ceremonial ice palace displayed for 30 winter nights.
